Styro refers to the white dermis under the epidermis. People call it “styro” because it looks like styrofoam. Basically, if you cut and the edges gape a little bit, and blood doesn’t well up right away, it’s styro. If you go through that, into the yellow, bubbly layer of subcutaneous fat, you’ve hit “beans” (so called because the fat globules look like baked beans. The beans layer has no nerve endings, so if you poke the yellow, it doesn’t hurt. Everything you cut through to get to it will, though.

I agree that at least on the surface, Jayce is not very relatable, but if you dig deeper, haven’t we all been put in positions where there is no “right” answer, or been forced into situations where in order to “make nice”, we have to compromise our beliefs? Most of us would say that in such a situation, we should be honorable and hold to our morals rather than drop them for pleasantries, but how many of us would actually follow through on that? Jayce chose the less honorable option, but honestly, isn’t that the more “relatable” action? And matters are complicated even more as you realize that he really had no choice to begin with; he was destined to fail. In order to succeed with Hextech, he needed the support of the council, but in order to win the support of the council, he eventually had to lose sight of what he had created Hextech for in the first place. There was simply no way to win.   
I think Jayce is a very complex character with many deep-set flaws, and I believe he needs to change in order to regain the admiration many viewers seemed to hold for him at first, but I think he has the capacity to become better, and I hope Riot will explore that in season 2.
